description: Fetch article content as clean plain text. Without section_index: returns the full article with == Section == markers preserved for structure — or, when the article exceeds the size budget, a compact section outline (truncated: true) that points to wikipedia_get_sections plus a section_index read instead of the full text. With section_index (from wikipedia_get_sections): returns that section and every subsection nested under it, each heading above its own body. section_index 0 is the lead section, the text above the first heading, which is the full prose wikipedia_get_summary returns only a truncated fragment of. Section-targeted reads are faster and smaller when only part of the article is needed. Both paths keep superscripts and subscripts apart from the text beside them (10²³, H₂O), render each formula as linear text (e^(iπ) + 1 = 0), or as TeX on a wiki that still serves it, with a display formula on a line of its own, render code samples as fenced blocks with their indentation intact, and render list items as "- " or numbered "N." lines indented two spaces per nesting level, the indent capped at 16 levels. A section read also renders data tables as pipe-delimited rows (header row first) and infoboxes as "label: value" lines; a table too large to include leaves a "[table omitted: N rows (table T)]" marker. Pass table_index: T with section_index to read only that table, limit whole rows per page; each page repeats the section parse, so read a whole table in as few pages as it allows by passing a limit up to table_rows (at most 500 per page). Follow next_cursor as cursor with the same inputs to continue at the pinned revision; the caption opens the first page, and every later page of a wikitable repeats its header row and delimiter. The full-article path carries no data tables or infoboxes, so read the section for those. Phylogenetic clade trees render as fenced, indented branches, with unnamed forks preserved; unparseable trees leave "[table omitted: unparseable clade]". Clade trees have no table_index. In a section read, tables used only for layout, such as multi-column lists, keep their content as ordinary text; the full-article path drops them, so read the section for those lists. Page furniture is omitted as well — maintenance banners, sister-project and library-resource boxes, portal bars, and spoken-article notices — while a hatnote naming a related article is kept. Every read returns the canonical article URL and the ID of the revision it was read from, for citation; a full read also returns that revision's timestamp. Redirect pages are followed automatically, and the citation fields name the target article.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous table page. Keep title, language, section_index and table_index unchanged. The cursor carries no variant, so pass variant on every page it should convert. Empty means the first page.

limit.description: Rows per page of a table read (default 25), counted from row_offset; the header row is row 0 of the first page. Requires table_index. Positive integers above 500 are clamped with a notice. Each call's limit sizes its own page, so it may change between pages.

section_index.description: Section index from wikipedia_get_sections. 0 reads the lead section (Introduction) — the text above the first heading. Omit for the full article. Providing this returns the targeted section plus every subsection nested under it, as plain text.

table_index.description: 1-based outer wikitable or infobox ordinal in the section. Requires section_index. Returns only that table in complete row pages; nested cell tables have no ordinal.

title.description: Article title (e.g. "Python (programming language)"). A trailing #fragment is accepted and ignored; the characters < > [ ] { } and | cannot appear in a Wikipedia page name. Special: and Media: titles, and interwiki links such as "wikt:cat", name no page.

variant.description: Script variant to convert the returned text to, on an edition with a language converter: "zh-hans", "zh-hant", "zh-cn", or "zh-tw" on zh; "sr-ec" (Cyrillic) or "sr-el" (Latin) on sr; "uz-latn" or "uz-cyrl" on uz. Pass the edition as language and the variant here. Matched case-insensitively against the edition's own list; an edition without a converter, such as en, accepts none. Omit it, or pass "", to read the text as stored. title and the other identifiers stay as stored, so title still chains into other calls.

name: wikipedia_get_article

content.description: Plain-text article content. Both full articles and section reads carry == Section == markers above the text each one heads, code samples as ``` fenced blocks, list items as "- " or "N." lines indented two spaces per nesting level, and superscripts and subscripts as Unicode characters (10²³, H₂O), or as ^x / ^(…) and _x / _(…) where a character has none. Formulas read as linear text in that notation (TeX on a wiki that still serves it), with a/b for a fraction (set apart by a space from what it multiplies: 1/2 (a + b)), √(…) for a root, and parentheses grouping a numerator, denominator, or script of more than one part (x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a)); a display formula stands on a line of its own, as does each row of a displayed system of equations, and an inline formula stays in its sentence. Section reads also carry data tables as | cell | cell | rows with a | --- | row under the header. When truncated is true, this instead carries a section outline (heading names and byte sizes) plus a pointer to the targeted-read path.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_table`: A table selector is unavailable, or section_index/table_index is missing for a table read, a cursor, or a limit. `invalid_cursor`: A table cursor is malformed, mismatched, or points past the pinned table. `revision_unavailable`: The table revision the cursor is pinned to no longer exists, is hidden, or cannot be read or verified. `not_found`: No Wikipedia article exists for the given title. `invalid_title`: The title can name no page: it contains characters MediaWiki forbids in a page name, is a Special: or Media: title in any edition's spelling, or is an interwiki link such as "wikt:cat". `invalid_section`: The section_index is out of range for this article. `invalid_language`: The language is not a valid BCP 47 code, or names a Wikipedia edition that does not exist. `invalid_variant`: The variant is not one the language edition converts to, or the edition has no script variants. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

last_modified.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of that revision, for dating the content. Full-article reads only; a section read carries none.

next_cursor.description: Pass unchanged as cursor with the same table request to read the pinned revision. Absent on the final page.

notice.description: Disambiguation-page guidance, redirect guidance, disclosure that an optional lookup (TOC verification, the disambiguation check) was unavailable, or that a table read clamped limit.

original_length.description: Character length of the full article text before outlining. Present only when truncated is true.

page_type.description: Present only on a disambiguation page — one that lists the articles a title can refer to — and then "disambiguation", the value wikipedia_get_summary reports for it.

pageid.description: Wikipedia page ID. Absent on API parse responses that omit it.

redirect_section.description: Redirect target fragment, or its normalized heading when verified. Explicit section_index still controls the read.

redirected_from.description: Original alias followed to the resolved article.

revision_id.description: ID of the revision the content was read from. "https://<edition>.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=<revision_id>" is a permanent link to exactly that version.

row_offset.description: Zero-based position of the first row this page counts.

rows_returned.description: Complete rows this page counts toward limit; the header row a continuation page repeats is not one of them.

section_title.description: Section title when section_index was provided — "Introduction" for the lead, which has no heading of its own. Absent for full-article reads.

sections_suggested.description: True when content is an outline — use its verified section_index values with wikipedia_get_article, or call wikipedia_get_sections for unindexed entries. Present only when truncated is true.

table_continued.description: True on pages after the first, which carry no caption; a wikitable continuation page repeats the header row and delimiter above its rows.

table_count.description: Available outer data tables in the pinned section.

table_index.description: Selected table ordinal, for table reads only.

table_rows.description: Total rendered rows, including the first header row.

truncated.description: True when a full-article read exceeded the size budget and content is a section outline instead of the full text. Always false for section reads and for full articles within budget.

url.description: Canonical desktop URL of the article (e.g. "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower"), for citing the page rather than composing a URL from the title.

variant.description: Script variant the text was converted to, spelled as the edition lists it ("zh-cn" for "zh-CN"). Absent when no variant was requested.

title: Get Wikipedia Article
